chunks: Hannan, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended the pulpit on the day of the conquest of Mecca and said: 'O people! Allah has removed from you the pride of ignorance and its boasting about forefathers. Indeed, you are from Adam (peace be upon him), and Adam is from clay. Indeed, the best of the servants of Allah is the one who is most pious. Arabic is not by a father and mother, but it is a speaking tongue. So whoever is deficient in his deeds, his lineage will not avail him. Indeed, every blood [shed] that was in the era of ignorance, or feud—and the feud is enmity—is under my foot here until the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.خَيْرَ عِبَادِ اللَّهِ: The best of the servants of Allah

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about lineage and pride on the day of the Conquest of Mecca?
ai.summary: Delivered at the pivotal moment of the Conquest of Mecca, this sermon by Imam al-Sadiq (as) via Hanan underscores the transition from tribal aristocracy to a meritocratic community based on Taqwa. It explicitly distinguishes between 'Arabia' as a linguistic marker rather than a genealogical privilege, thereby nullifying pre-Islamic blood feuds (Ihnah) and establishing spiritual equality under divine authority.
